instructions: Begin visible teaching with the lesson purpose and why it matters, the first person and decision, the teaching-to-practice sequence and the exact final product. Establish this orientation before a numerical hook, technical exposition or dense case record; a collapsed roadmap does not substitute for it.
Introduce the fictional person, goal and constraints before referring to their evidence. Define document types, technical terms and shorthand when first needed.
Explain a useful basic idea before presenting dense case records or asking a decision. Integrate case-specific explanation beside the lines it interprets.
Write one connected manuscript before implementation. Replace repetitive or superseded passages; connect each section to the unresolved question from the previous one.
Model the action and why it matters: locate relevant evidence, interpret it, calculate when appropriate, state what follows and what remains uncertain.
Keep calculation units, repeated and once-only amounts, exclusions, rounding conventions and dates visible. Explain the meaning of the result for this person.

Introduce supported practice as a controlled change: identify what stays the same, what changes, the fields to use and how feedback helps revision. Do not give the selection answer in the task lead-in.
Introduce independent work as a new application: name the new person and records, identify which method transfers, and align prompt, labels, model and signoffs.
Give existing videos, transcripts, handouts and tools a specific viewing/reading/experiment purpose. Connect their point to the next learner action; retain professional sources.
Keep essential teaching and task requirements visible. Retain approved numbered instructions plus initially collapsed additional guidance, hints and deliberate model reveals.
Use CALM native typography, colours, sidebar, document presentation and stacked core-vocabulary disclosure. Dotted-underlined words use the existing keyboard-accessible popup.
Close by answering the opening question and explaining the next lesson connection. Respect alternative defensible responses while explaining the evidence limits.
Preserve outcomes, original task facts, controls, IDs, answer keys, task versions, media, history, completion and namespaces. Flag task changes separately before any migration.
Every required course activity remains possible with supplied information. Do not add teacher contact, outside account, personal disclosure, real transaction or supervised experience dependencies.

For Alberta course planning, distinguish diploma requirements from program entry preparation. Use verified real course names/prerequisites and actual credit values; label invented people, offerings, fees and program conditions. A partial pathway exercise must not claim to be a complete graduation audit.
